key_insight: A 190 mm spray distance produced the densest Cr3C2–NiCr coating and the best corrosion resistance on DSS 2205 in 1 M H2SO4.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing D-gun spray distance is a practical lever for improving coating integrity, reducing porosity, and extending corrosion protection in acidic industrial service.
method: D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm
Evaluated corrosion behavior in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, EIS, and potentiodynamic polarization
Compared SEM morphology, porosity, and corrosion rate across spray distances
evidence_signal: Porosity decreased from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm, and the 190 mm coating showed the lowest corrosion rate at 0.113 mmpy versus 2.60 mmpy for the uncoated substrate.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on a single acidic electrolyte and room-temperature testing, so performance may differ under other chemistries, temperatures, or long-term service conditions.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
